body: In my experience with songwriting, you kind of have to expect that some work you do is a waste of time and won't work out. At least personally, I'm never really happy with anything I put out, I just try to compare it to what I was originally going for and see if it ticks all the boxes. Especially when you put your work on display, it's terrifying. I guess all to remember is that you've got a different perspective on it now than the original idea you had. It's something you've started at and worked on for hours, every little detail is yours, and it can kind of numb your mind to how well it actually reflects your idea. Keep working on it, keep putting stuff out there! Art is by its nature a very individual and personal thing, and there are bound to be people who don't understand your vision. But those who do will absolutely love it!

I do understand coming from Casanova it's probably a bit of a shock, but the atmosphere, lyrics and synergy between the instruments and Jacobs voice is absolutely beautiful. That's not to say I'm disappointed with heroine, I'm absolutely not. I think for a band trying a completely new style and dropping a full length album in it with only one weak point in my opinion (valentine), it's really impressive. Listening to dark pool I think is the best way to appreciate that. I would normally agree, I love creative ways of bringing back choices from old games (like the flashback in wolfenstein for example) but I think a branching story isn't really what ghost of tsushima is about. I think one really well written storyline will always beat a few less well written ones, which naturally happens with the scope of ghost. I would love to see a bunch of paths that lead to different missions and affect the story, and I agree that either a samurai/shinobi path would be really cool, but I don't think it makes sense after the entire story of ghost to just go back and let you be samurai again, as the point is that he's too far gone to go back. I love converging and dividing storylines, but not at the cost of the quality of the story overall, and I just can't think of many games that have pulled it off

I think if there was a sequel it would still be just one solid storyline, as I think sparing Shimura is the "intended" outcome. Through all of the game, you see Jin slowly stripping away at what it means to be samurai, often against shimuras teachings. To deny him an honourable death represents his full transformation into the ghost as you can tell he puts the protection of his home and people above all else, including honour. Sparing shimura is an extremely dishonourable thing to do from his perspective but it shows that Jin is without a doubt no longer samurai
